subjective: Patient reports cough, cold, runny nose, muscle aches, occasional headache, chills for about five days.
Patient describes cough as dry, hacking.
Patient denies shortness of breath, wheeze, blood in sputum, chest pain, fever.
Patient reports taking paracetamol for pain.
Patient takes metformin for diabetes and lisinopril for blood pressure.
Patient has diabetes for five to six years; monitors blood sugars at home with normal readings.
Patient's last blood pressure reading was taken this morning and was within normal range.
objective: Mild redness at the back of the throat.
No palpable glands in the neck.
assessment: Clinician considers a viral upper respiratory infection (cold) with no evidence of chest infection.
plan: Patient advised to use over‑the‑counter symptomatic relief (Night Nurse, Day Nurse) which is compatible with current medications.
No prescription medication is required at this time.
Patient instructed to contact the service if shortness of breath, wheeze, or symptoms persist beyond three weeks or worsen.
